content_evidence.comparison: For each source file and returned get-page text, lowercase and tokenize ASCII alphanumerics; compute SHA-256 truncated to 20 hex digits of each seven-token window; discard the first 20 source tokens; compare sets. This is content evidence, NOT byte identity, exact metadata intent, or a valid Git source repair.

limits_and_disposition: Local work gbrain has content for all 20, but this rebuildable database is not authoritative Git source. The 20 malformed tracked Git pages remain invalid for the source-current gate.

All 19 get-page titles on pages with first H1 equal that H1; this could be derived metadata and does not independently prove author intent. The YAML_PARSE get-page title differs from the explicit Git-source title under basic normalization.

The get-page Source repo/File path fields can describe a cited source rather than the brain page’s Git origin; a first tested field disagreed with the brain Git remote/path despite complete content fingerprint overlap. They are not proof of source provenance.

No byte-preserved body boundary, intended ID/title for all 20, or safe repair candidate is established. No brain Git edit/ref/push, database/policy change, index/build/cutover, or routed write was performed. Joe’s prior generic repair grant does not authorize silently choosing conflicting metadata.

local_work_brain.method: For 19 pages, search the first source H1; for the YAML_PARSE page, search its explicit existing title. Select the unique namespaced result whose slug ends in the source filename stem, then run non-fuzzy exact gbrain get on that result. A bare source filename stem did not resolve by exact get in the first six tested; keyword hits and get-page provenance fields were not treated as identity proof.
